key_choices.text: Maresca dropped Guardiola's system of players voting for the captain. He chose to appoint the leadership group himself.
He named Rúben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma as City's four captains for 2026/27.
Maresca left Phil Foden out of the four-man captaincy group. He said Guéhi had been captain at Palace and Donnarumma captains Italy.
After pre-season he said 18-year-old winger Ryan McAidoo would likely stay with the first team this season. He described him as 'the kind of winger I love'.
He said three academy players would be part of his 2026/27 first-team squad, alongside around 20 senior players.

links.text: This is Maresca's third spell at City. He was Elite Development Squad coach (won the PL2 title in 2020/21), then Guardiola's assistant from June 2022, and is now head coach. He left Chelsea on 1 January 2026.

Chelsea said Maresca asked to leave mid-contract after being told of the City opportunity. Maresca said he 'unexpectedly and abruptly resigned' in December 2025, and that this was neither his intention nor his wish. Chelsea have since appointed Xabi Alonso, who was replaced at Real Madrid by Fulham's Arbeloa.

After the Crystal Palace defeat he shifted towards a more balanced approach on transitions. Fulham then drew 0-0 at Liverpool.
Arbeloa calls Calvin Bassey 'one of my captains'. Bassey also wore the armband in Fulham's last two pre-season games.
Arbeloa has backed younger attackers such as Bobb, Josh King and Gonzalo García, rather than the experienced forwards Fulham leaned on last season.

title_options: Man City 1-1 Fulham: 8 of 15 shots were blocked
Why Maresca's City could not beat Fulham
Maresca's City made the chances. Fulham made the blocks
script.description:
Manchester City 1-1 Fulham at the Etihad. City made the chances, Fulham scored first, and Elliot Anderson's volley saved a point. We follow Enzo Maresca, Anderson and Oscar Bobb, and ask one question: if City made the chances, why did they not win? The answer sits in what happened to their shots before they reached the goalkeeper. Sources quoted: BBC Sport, Yahoo Sports, AllFootballApp, Dave.sport, a VAVEL USA live blog and Manchester City's official site.

The Other Touchline: modern football, explained. What should Maresca change first? Tell us in the comments.

Data: football-data.org + FotMob.

shots.text: Etihad Stadium, Manchester. 60,038 people in the stands, and one question for Enzo Maresca. Can his City still win at home?
He is the man who followed Pep Guardiola, who left after 10 years. His side have lost 3 of their last 5. Fulham are the visitors.
It finishes 1-1. And City made more chances than Fulham. So this is Maresca's problem. His team made the chances... so why did they not win?

shots.text: Minute 24. Haaland, from close range, left foot. Saved. FotMob's expected goals, or xG, is learned from past shots, and says how often a chance like this is scored. This one is worth 0.7. About 7 in 10.
Minute 42. Dias heads a corner over from close range. Another big chance, gone. Fulham's goal came from a chance worth 0.14. City's best one was 5 times bigger.
Half-time: Fulham 1, City 0. Our reading: the turning point is not a goal. It is a chance not taken. City have the better of the chances, and still must find a way through.

shots.text: Now the opening question. xG: City 1.87, Fulham 0.74. So why only 1-1? One cause stands out.
Follow City's 15 shots. 8 were blocked. 4 more missed. Only 3 were on target, and 1 went in. Fulham's goalkeeper was not the hero: Leno's goals prevented is minus 0.54.
Our reading: 83 percent of City's danger came through the centre, and Fulham's defenders made 7 blocks to City's 1. That points to a crowded middle. The data cannot show where anyone stood.
Replay these chances 20,000 times and City win 69 in 100. They made enough. The wall took it away.

shots.text: So, the answer. City did not lack chances. They lacked a way through: 8 of their 15 shots were blocked. City are third on 22 points, but winless in four league games, says BBC Sport.
Our reading: Maresca's City can create. His test now is turning chances into shots that reach the goalkeeper. One match cannot prove a pattern.
What should Maresca change first? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to The Other Touchline.

notes: Scene 1 opens with "Manchester City are third in the table, but they arrive having lost 3 of their last 5 matches" and "a Fulham side with 2 wins and 5 draws", which is a table and form recap. Open on the human situation instead: Maresca, the first coach after Guardiola's 10 years, hosting a struggling side, and ask whether his City can still win at home.

Scene 1 gives away the result ("It ends 1-1") and then asks "what really cost them the win?" with no human stakes. Keep the question, but state it as Maresca's problem: City made the chances, so why did they not win?

Scene 3 ("Three people carry this story") spends its time on the reporter's double-pivot reading and a hedge ("That is the reporter's reading, not Maresca's words"). It is repeated and wooden, and Haaland is tacked on as a fourth character. Cut it to one line per character and give each a role in the story: Maresca under pressure, Anderson the rescuer, Bobb the assist-maker against a frustrated Haaland.

Scene 7 runs through chance quality, finishing, blocks, goalkeeping and luck as a checklist of stats (0.12 xG per shot, minus 0.87, 8 blocked, minus 0.54, 83 percent). It reads like a report and ends on "the numbers cannot rank blocks against finishing", so the opening question never gets an answer. Pick one cause that the data supports best, such as 8 of 15 shots blocked with only 3 on target, and build the reveal around it.

Scene 6 jumps from the equaliser to the swing around minute 70 and ends on "They cannot say why". The story stalls at its turning point. Cut the "80 percent / 27 percent" momentum line, or tie it to what happened next so it moves the story on, and do not end the scene on a shrug.

The ending ("Was this finishing, or a defence that did exactly enough?") hands the question back to the viewer. Also, "A draw was a less likely result than a City win" is a weak point, since 69 percent to 21 percent is plain. Close with one clear answer to the opening question, tied to Maresca's first big test, and keep the comment prompt as a light add-on.

shorts.title: Anderson's 3% volley saved City a point

shots.text: 8.1 rating. A 3% chance. A goal.
Elliot Anderson was the best-rated player on the pitch.
At minute 57, City trailed 1-0. His right-foot shot, from a corner, had an expected goals value of 0.03. It went in.
He also had 4 shots, created 3 chances and made 9 defensive actions, as one of City's two deep midfielders.
He lost 9 duels and was dispossessed 3 times, so not flawless. But he saved a point on a night Haaland, with 1.03 xG, scored none.
Is Anderson City's most important midfielder right now? Full story on the channel.

shorts.title: Minute 70: when Man City's grip on Fulham broke

shots.text: Minute 70 changed how this match felt.
Before it, City had taken 14 of their 15 shots. They had trailed since minute 16 and equalised at 57.
Then both coaches changed things. City swapped Foden for Cherki. Fulham brought on Robinson and Larsson.
City had been on top in 80% of the 15 minutes before. In the 15 after, only 27%. They took one more shot all game, blocked, worth 0.05 xG.
The numbers show the swing, not whether the changes caused it. On chance quality, City won 69% of 20,000 replays. A draw came in 21%.
Did the substitutions cost City the win? Full story on the channel.
